newsitem.title: USA: XLConnect drags down Intelligent Electronics.
newsitem.headline: XLConnect drags down Intelligent Electronics.

text.p: XLConnect Solutions Inc's share price dropped sharply Friday after a dismal earnings forecast and pulled down shares of its majority shareholder, Intelligent Electronics Inc.
XLConnect, which makes network products for computer and communications systems, fell 14 points to 9-5/8 in heavy trading.
Intelligent Electronics, which holds an 82.1 percent stake in XLConnect, fell 3-5/8 to 4 and was one of the most heavily traded Nasdaq issues.
XLConnect said Friday it expects to earn $0.02-$0.04 a share on revenues of $30-$32 million in the fourth quarter, falling short of analysts' earnings expectations.
According to First Call, analysts' consensus earnings estimate for XLConnect is $0.09 a share in the quarter.
XLConnect cited temporary delays in several large projects, unexpected plant shutdowns by several major outsourced desktop clients over the holidays, and fewer working days during the period.
The Exton, Pa.-based company said it expects growth to accelerate during the 1997 first half as it continues to develop its internal sales force.

XLConnect soared in its initial public offering in October, when it was spun off from Intelligent Electronics. The stock reached a high of 31-3/4, with analysts predicting strong demand for the company's products and shares.
XLConnect also said Chief Executive Richard Ellenberger was seeking to negotiate his departure from the firm.
Alex. Brown on Friday downgraded XLConnect to neutral from buy.
